failure_mode: Shared fibre/switch becomes a common-cause failure path for PROFINET control and SWS monitoring on side A (fibre break, switch power loss, switch firmware fault, SFP failure take out both at once)
effect: Hoist control and SWS data are lost together. If SWS is credited as an independent protection or monitoring layer for the hoists, that independence is lost and the layer-of-protection argument in the FMECA no longer holds; if SWS is logging only, the effect is loss of event evidence during the very event that caused the outage.
cause: Design decision to route SWS logger traffic over the PROFINET fibre instead of a physically separate path; the draft does not state whether SWS is safety-related or logging-only, so the independence requirement has not been checked.

failure_mode: Logger VLAN uplink creates a new ingress path into the side A control switches (remote logger server, shore link, maintenance laptop on a base-station port)
effect: Unauthorised or faulty traffic from outside the hoist network reaches the shared switches; VLAN hopping, switch management-plane exposure or switch CPU load can disturb PROFINET even though the PLC VLAN is nominally segregated.
cause: The logger uplink destination and its network zone are not defined; the draft specifies VLAN segregation but no firewall/data-diode, no management-plane hardening, and no zone/conduit assessment for the new connection.

failure_mode: Storm-control, rate-limit, port-security and VLAN settings on the shared switches are lost or reverted (switch replacement, factory reset, firmware update, manual change during commissioning or service)
effect: The two mitigations that answer DEMO-NET-001 and DEMO-NET-002 silently stop existing; SWS traffic can again storm or reach the PLC VLAN with no alarm.
cause: Mitigation implemented purely in switch configuration with no configuration management, backup/restore procedure, change control or periodic verification defined in the draft.

failure_mode: Storm control or ingress rate limit intended for base-station ports is applied switch-wide or copied to PROFINET ports (template, global setting, wrong port in config)
effect: Legitimate PROFINET multicast/broadcast (DCP, MRP test frames, alarms) is rate-limited or the PROFINET port is disabled on exceedance; devices drop off the bus or the redundancy ring fails to reconfigure.
cause: Draft specifies the mitigation per port but gives no rule that PROFINET and ring ports are excluded, and no test that verifies this after configuration.

failure_mode: Ingress limit sized to the 100 kbps average (DEMO) trips on a legitimate burst, e.g. base station flushing buffered logger data after an RS-485 or fibre interruption, and the port is disabled
effect: Loss of SWS data for that hoist until someone manually re-enables the port; if auto-recovery is enabled, the port flaps and data is lost repeatedly. The outage is self-inflicted by the mitigation and may coincide with the event that should have been logged.
cause: Rate limit set on average rather than peak traffic; base-station buffering/retry behaviour not characterised; recovery action after port shutdown not defined.

failure_mode: Base-station port wrongly included in the MRP/MRPD ring domain or base station loops two ports (misplaced patch cord)
effect: Ring topology change or loop on the PROFINET side; reconfiguration storms or ring failure affect hoist control on side A.
cause: Fibre topology and redundancy scheme not supplied; draft notes it must be confirmed but no register row or test covers it.
